The present regulation establishes the "Act for European Security through Strengthening of the European Defence Industry" instrument (hereinafter referred to as the "SAFE instrument"), which provides Member States with financial assistance by enabling them to make urgent and important public investments in support of the European defence industry in light of the current crisis situation.

The present regulation defines the conditions and procedures under which financial assistance under the SAFE instrument is provided to Member States and implemented by them, and sets the rules concerning simplified and accelerated joint acquisition procedures for the purchase of defence products and other products intended for defence purposes falling within the following categories:

a) first category: ammunition and missiles; artillery systems, including deep precision strike capabilities; ground combat capabilities and their support systems, including soldier equipment and infantry weapons; small drones (NATO class 1) and related counter-drone systems; critical infrastructure protection; cyber domain; and military mobility, including counter-mobility;

b) second category: air defense and anti-missile systems; surface and submarine maritime capabilities; drones other than small drones (NATO classes 2 and 3) and related counter-drone systems; strategic means such as, but not limited to, strategic airlift, aerial refueling, C4 ISTAR systems, as well as space means and services; protection of space assets; artificial intelligence and electronic warfare.
For the purposes of this regulation, the following terms mean:
"defense products," goods, services, and works that fall within the scope of application of Directive 2009/81/EC, as defined in Article 2 of said Directive;

"other products intended for defense purposes," goods, services, and works other than those falling within the scope of the application of Directive 2009/81/EC, as defined in Article 2 of that Directive, which are necessary or dedicated to defense purposes;

3) "joint acquisition", the procurement procedure for defense products or other products intended for defense purposes and the resulting public contracts, implemented by at least one Member State benefiting from financial assistance under the Instrument for Stability and Peace (SAFE) and another Member State, or one of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) States that are members of the European Economic Area (EEA), or Ukraine. Furthermore, joint acquisition may include countries in the process of accession, candidate countries, potential candidates, as well as other third countries with which the Union has concluded a security and defense partnership (non-binding instrument). Joint acquisitions can also include existing contracts that meet the same conditions.
The SAFE instrument complements the measures taken by the Union and the Member States to finance urgent and important public investments in support of the European defense industry.

A Member State may request financial assistance under the SAFE instrument (hereinafter referred to as "financial assistance") for activities, expenses, and measures aimed at addressing the crisis situation referred to in Article 1. These activities, expenses, and measures are related to defense products or other products intended for defense purposes and implemented within the framework of joint acquisitions carried out in accordance with the eligibility rules set out in Article 16, with the aim of:
to accelerate the adaptation of the defense industry to structural changes, including by creating or enhancing its production capabilities as well as related support activities;

to improve the timely availability of defense products, including by reducing their delivery times, reserving production slots, or building up stocks of defense products, intermediate products, or raw materials; or
c) ensure interoperability and interchangeability throughout the Union.

2. A Member State may use financial assistance under the SAFE instrument in synergy with Union programs in accordance with the rules of those programs. Financial assistance under the SAFE instrument may also be used to finance activities that have benefited from Union funding under a Union program.

3. Notwithstanding paragraph 1 of this Article, acquisitions carried out by a Member State may benefit from support under the SAFE instrument where a public procurement contract has been signed no later than 30 May 2026. Where a Member State includes such an acquisition in the plan referred to in Article 7(2), it shall take all necessary steps actively to extend the benefit of the relevant market to at least one other Member State, an EFTA member State of the EEA, or Ukraine, in addition to any potential candidate country or third country partner interested in the matter with which the Union has concluded a security and defence partnership. The eligibility criteria laid down in Article 16(2) to (14) shall apply mutatis mutandis.
Financial assistance takes the form of a loan granted by the Union to the concerned member state.
The maximum amount of financial assistance in the form of loans granted under the SAFE instrument is 150 000 000 000 EUR.

Each Member State wishing to benefit from financial assistance under the SAFE instrument shall submit a request for this purpose to the Commission no later than November 30, 2025. The request is accompanied by an investment plan for the European Defense Industry (hereinafter referred to as the "plan").
The plan is properly motivated and supported. It includes the following elements:
a) a description of the needs for defense products and other products intended for defense purposes;
b) a description of the activities, estimated expenses, and measures planned in accordance with Article 4;
c) if applicable, a description of the envisaged participation of Ukraine in the activities, expenses, and measures foreseen, or of the actions planned in favor of Ukraine;
d) a description of the measures planned to ensure that Article 16 and the procurement rules are respected, including a description of how compliance must be ensured.

Where appropriate, Member States include a description of activities aimed at enhancing supply chain security and resilience, including by facilitating access for SMEs, mid-cap companies, and new entrants to the defense market.

When drawing up their plans, member states may request the Commission to organize an exchange of best practices and, where appropriate, to seek synergies with other member states' defense industry investment plans, so that member states making such a request can benefit from the experience of other member states.

5. Member States may submit to the Commission a revised request for financial assistance accompanied by a modified version of the plan where this is duly justified by changes in the planned expenditures or measures, subject to the availability of loan amounts.
The Commission evaluates the financial assistance request along with the plan as soon as possible.

When the Commission finds that the application meets the conditions set out in this Regulation, including those laid down in Article 4, Article 7(2), and Article 16, it submits a proposal for a Council implementing decision to make financial assistance available.
3. The act of the Council referred to in paragraph 2 shall include the following elements:
a) confirmation that the request referred to in Article 7(1) meets the conditions set out in this regulation; and
b) the amount of the loan and the amount of support in the form of a loan to be paid as an advance payment in accordance with Article 11.
In all cases, the Commission communicates its assessment of the application to the concerned Member State and justifies its assessment.

5. When it presents the proposal to the Council in accordance with paragraph 2, the Commission examines the existing and anticipated financing needs of the requesting Member State as well as the requests for financial assistance under this Regulation that other Member States have already submitted or intend to submit, while applying the principles of equal treatment, solidarity, proportionality, and transparency. This proposal is presented at the earliest opportunity.
6. The Council is to adopt the implementing decision referred to in paragraph 2, in principle, within four weeks of the adoption of the Commission's proposal.

7. When, following the adoption of the implementing decision under paragraph 2, amounts remain available for financial assistance under the SAFE instrument, the Commission may publish a new call for expressions of interest no later than 31 December 2026. In such a case, the procedure laid down in Article 7 and paragraphs 1 to 5 of this Article shall apply mutatis mutandis.
8. A decision to implement under paragraph 2 shall be adopted by no later than June 30, 2027.

In order to finance the support granted under the SAFE instrument in the form of loans, the Commission is empowered, on behalf of the Union, to borrow the necessary funds from capital markets or financial institutions in accordance with Article 224 of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 (hereinafter referred to as the "financial regulation").
2. Borrowing and lending operations under the SAFE instrument are conducted in euros.
As soon as a Council implementing decision referred to in Article 8(2) is adopted, the Commission concludes a loan agreement and operational arrangements with the requesting Member State.

2. The loan agreement defines the period of availability and the detailed terms of the support provided under the SAFE instrument in the form of loans. The loan agreement has a maximum duration of forty-five years. In addition to the elements set out in Article 223, paragraph 4, of the Financial Regulation, the loan agreement includes the amount of pre-financing and the rules regarding the repayment of the pre-financing.

3. Operational arrangements define the relationship between the implementation of a plan and the corresponding financial assistance, including a provisional schedule for disbursements of loan tranches, accompanied, where appropriate, by annual ceilings. Additionally, these operational arrangements define the types of documentary evidence and control rules regarding compliance with the specific eligibility criteria applied by member states in accordance with Article 16, as well as the detailed elements referred to in Article 14.
Member States may request, as part of their plan, an advance payment of up to a maximum of 15% of the support in the form of a loan.

2. The advance payment is subject to the entry into force of the loan agreement referred to in Article 10, paragraph 2. The loan agreement may provide that the advance payment is conditional upon the completion of the operational arrangements referred to in Article 10, paragraph 3.
3. Payments are made subject to the availability of funds. The advance financing may be paid in one lump sum or in several staggered installments.

The period during which the loan is available, which corresponds to the period during which disbursements may be approved under this Article in favor of the relevant Member State, expires on December 31, 2030. Disbursements will be made in tranches, subject to the availability of funds. A tranche may be paid in one lump sum or in several phased payments.

2. The concerned Member State may submit to the Commission a duly justified payment request. Such a payment request may be submitted by the concerned Member State to the Commission twice a year. The Member State justifies the payment request by providing evidence of progress made in implementing the plan.

3. The Commission evaluates the completeness, accuracy, and consistency of the claim referred to in paragraph 2 as soon as possible, and no later than within two months of receiving the request. When the result of its assessment of compliance with the conditions set out in this regulation is positive, the Commission adopts as soon as possible a decision authorizing the disbursement of the loan tranche.

4. If, following the assessment referred to in paragraph 3, the Commission concludes that the payment claim referred to in paragraph 2 is unsatisfactory, the disbursement of all or part of the loan shall be suspended. The concerned Member State may submit its comments within one month of the notification of the assessment made by the Commission.

5. The Commission evaluates the observations referred to in paragraph 4 as soon as possible. It lifts the suspension when the concerned Member State has demonstrated that it has taken the necessary measures to ensure satisfactory compliance with the conditions laid down in this Regulation.
The share of loans granted to the three Member States that are the largest recipients of such loans does not exceed 60% of the maximum amount referred to in Article 6.
The loan agreement includes the necessary provisions regarding controls and audits required by Article 223, paragraph 4, of the Financial Regulation.
The Commission presents to the European Parliament and the Council an annual report on the use of financial assistance.
If appropriate, the report is accompanied by a proposal to extend the period of availability of the SAFE instrument.
Joint acquisitions are eligible for support under the SAFE instrument only if they meet the eligibility criteria set out in this article.

2. The procedures and joint acquisition markets for defense products include the participation requirements for contractors and subcontractors participating in a joint acquisition as set forth in paragraphs 3 to 13 and 15 of this Article, without prejudice to the conditions established by the agreements referred to in Article 17.

3. The contractors and subcontractors participating in the joint acquisition are established in the Union, in an EEA member EFTA State, or in Ukraine, and have their executive management structures there. They are not subject to the control of a third country that is neither an EEA member EFTA State nor Ukraine, nor of an entity of another third country that is not established in the Union, in an EEA member EFTA State, or in Ukraine.

4. By derogation from paragraph 3, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with third-country partners, joint acquisitions involving a subcontractor to which between 15% and 35% of the market value has been attributed, and which is not established in the Union, in an EFTA member State of the EEA or in Ukraine, or does not have its management execution structures there, shall only be eligible for support under the SAFE instrument if at least one of the following conditions is met:
a) a direct contractual relationship related to the defense product was established between the contractor and the aforementioned subcontractor before the effective date of this regulation;

b) the contractor commits to studying, within a two-year period, the possibility of replacing the inputs provided by the aforementioned subcontractor with an input free from any original restriction of the Union, an EEA member state, or Ukraine, and meeting the technical and timing requirements.

5. Notwithstanding paragraph 3, a legal entity established in the Union and controlled by a third country or by an entity of a third country may participate in a joint acquisition if it has undergone screening under Regulation (EU) 2019/452 and, where necessary, appropriate mitigation measures, or if it provides verified guarantees by the Member State in which the contracting party or subcontractor participating in the joint acquisition is established. The guarantees provide assurances that the participation of the contracting party or subcontractor in the joint acquisition does not run counter to the Union’s and its Member States' interests in terms of security and defense as defined within the framework of the Common Foreign and Security Policy pursuant to Title V of the Treaty on the European Union.

6. The guarantees referred to in paragraph 5 may be based on a standardized model provided by the Commission and form part of the tender documentation, in order to ensure harmonized use throughout the Union. These guarantees, in particular, attest that measures are in place to ensure that, for the purposes of a joint acquisition, the following is secured:
a) control over the contractor or subcontractor participating in the joint acquisition is not exercised in a manner that limits or restricts its ability to fulfill the order and produce results; and

b) a third country or a third-country entity may not have access to the classified information related to the joint acquisition, and the employees or other individuals participating in the joint acquisition must hold a national security clearance issued by a Member State in accordance with national legislative and regulatory provisions.

7. The contracting authority carrying out a joint procurement shall submit to the Commission a notification concerning the mitigation measures applied in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/452 or the guarantees referred to in paragraph 5. Additional information on the mitigation measures applied or the guarantees shall be made available to the Commission at its request.

8. The infrastructure, facilities, assets, and resources of contractors and subcontractors participating in a joint acquisition that are used for the purposes of the joint acquisition must be located on the territory of an EU member state, an EEA member state of the EFTA, or Ukraine. When the contractors or subcontractors participating in the joint acquisition do not have readily available alternative solutions or relevant infrastructure, facilities, assets, and resources on the territory of an EU member state, an EEA member state of the EFTA, or Ukraine, they may use their infrastructure, facilities, assets, and resources that are situated or held outside these territories, provided that such use does not prejudice the Union and its member states' interests in terms of security and defense.

9. Contractors and subcontractors participating in joint acquisitions may be considered as meeting the eligibility criteria set out in paragraphs 3 to 7 when they have fulfilled equivalent conditions under Regulations (EU) 2018/1092 (9), (EU) 2021/697 (10), (EU) 2023/1525 or (EU) 2023/2418 of the European Parliament and of the Council, provided that no subsequent amendment undermines compliance with these conditions.

10. The cost of components whose origin is outside the Union, the EEA EFTA States, and Ukraine does not exceed 35% of the estimated cost of the final product's components. For joint procurements benefiting from support under the SAFE instrument, no component comes from any other third country that runs counter to the Union and its Member States' interests in terms of security and defense.

For products of the second category of defense items referred to in Article 1, second paragraph, point b), the contractors have the ability to decide, without restrictions imposed by third countries or by entities of third countries, on the definition, adaptation, and evolution of the design of the acquired defense product, including the legal authority to replace or remove components that are subject to restrictions imposed by third countries or by entities of third countries.

For the purposes of this Article, "participating subcontractor in a joint acquisition" means any legal entity that provides critical inputs with unique attributes essential to the functioning of a product, which is allocated at least 15% of the market value, and which requires access to classified information for the execution of the market.

13. The Member States ensure that the procurement procedures and markets for other products intended for defense purposes resulting from joint acquisitions benefiting from support under the SAFE instrument include appropriate eligibility criteria to protect the security and defense interests of the Union and its Member States.

14. The Member States shall specify in the plan referred to in Article 7 the eligibility criteria in accordance with paragraphs 3 to 11 and 13 to 15 of this Article, without prejudice to any conditions laid down in the agreements referred to in Article 17. Financial assistance is conditional upon the submission, together with the payment request, of the information indicated in the operational arrangements referred to in Article 10.

15. Member States may use the financial assistance provided under the SAFE instrument to finance their participation in the procedures for jointly organized acquisitions pursuant to Article 168, paragraphs 2 or 3, of the Financial Regulation. In such cases, and notwithstanding Article 168, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Financial Regulation, third countries participating in the joint acquisition may also participate in any procurement mechanism provided for in Article 168, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Financial Regulation and benefit from it.

The Union may conclude bilateral or multilateral agreements with accession countries, potential candidate countries, and candidates other than Ukraine, as well as other third countries with which the Union has concluded a security and defense partnership (non-binding instrument), in order to extend to these countries and their territories the eligibility conditions referred to in Article 16, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article.
2. The bilateral or multilateral agreement referred to in paragraph 1 specifies how the eligibility criteria set out in Article 16 should be applied. In particular, it sets out:

the conditions and terms related to the participation of contractors and subcontractors established in the third country in a joint acquisition under the SAFE instrument, including the conditions related to the localization of executive management structures and the control exercised by third countries or entities of third countries;

b) the rules regarding the location of contractors' or subcontractors' infrastructure, facilities, assets, and resources participating in a joint procurement that are used for the manufacture of defense products or other products intended for defense purposes provided under markets resulting from joint procurements under the SAFE instrument;

c) the rules regarding the cost of third-country components, including a minimum share of components originating in the Union, an EEA member country of the EFTA, or Ukraine, and a maximum share of components not originating in the Union, an EEA member country of the EFTA, Ukraine, or a third country party to the agreement;

d) the rules regarding restrictions imposed by third countries that are not parties to the agreement or by entities established in their territory, concerning the definition, adaptation, and evolution of the acquired defense product's design with the support of the SAFE instrument.
3. The bilateral or multilateral agreement:
to ensure a fair balance regarding the third country's contributions and benefits;
sets the conditions for any financial contribution that the third country must provide to the Union;
c) establishes any other appropriate measure governing the security of supply of the acquired product;
d) contributes to increased standardization of defense systems and greater interoperability between the capabilities of member states and those other third countries.

4. The contributions referred to in paragraph 3(b) constitute external assigned revenues in accordance with Article 21(5) of the Financial Regulation and are used for programs supporting the Union's defense industry, Ukraine's defense industry, and Ukraine in accordance with the rules of those programs.

When an acquisition benefits from support under the SAFE instrument, the rules set out in paragraphs 2 to 4 apply to a framework agreement or existing contract for the purchase of defense goods that is at least partially financed by one of the participating Member States using the loan granted under the SAFE instrument and does not provide the possibility of substantially modifying it. When applying paragraphs 2 and 3, the contracting authority that has concluded the framework agreement or contract obtains the prior agreement of the company with which it has concluded such framework agreement or contract.

2. A contracting authority of a Member State may amend a framework agreement or existing contract relating to defence goods where such framework agreement or contract was concluded with an enterprise meeting the criteria laid down in Article 16(3) to (13) of this Regulation, in order to add new contracting authorities participating in an acquisition as parties to that framework agreement or contract. The first subparagraph of Article 29(2) of Directive 2009/81/EU shall not apply to contracting authorities which were not originally parties to the framework agreement or contract.

By way of derogation from Article 29(2)(3) of Directive 2009/81/EC, a contracting authority of a Member State may make substantial modifications to the quantities set out in a framework agreement or a contract whose estimated value exceeds the thresholds laid down in Article 8 of Directive 2009/81/EC, where that framework agreement or contract was concluded with an entity meeting the criteria equivalent to those set out in Article 16(3) to (13) of this Regulation, and to the extent that such modification is strictly necessary for the application of paragraph 2 of this Article.
For the purpose of calculating the value referred to in paragraph 3, the adjusted value shall be the reference point where the market includes an indexing clause.

5. A contracting authority that has amended a framework contract or a contract as referred to in paragraphs 2 or 3 of this Article shall publish notice of such amendment in the Official Journal of the European Union in accordance with Article 32 of Directive 2009/81/EC.

In the cases referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3, the principle of equality of rights and obligations applies between the contracting authorities that are parties to the framework agreement or the contract, particularly regarding the cost of additional quantities acquired.

Acquisitions in which at least one Member State benefiting from financial assistance under the ESM Framework Agreement participate shall be deemed to satisfy the urgency condition resulting from crisis situations for the purposes of Article 28, paragraph 1 (c), of Directive 2009/81/EU.

For the purposes of this regulation, supplies, intra-Community acquisitions, and imports of defense goods or other products intended for defense purposes that are carried out in the context of contracts resulting from procurements benefiting from support under the SAFE instrument are exempt from value added tax (VAT) applicable under Council Directive 2006/112/EC. The exemption is understood to include entitlement to deduct VAT paid at the previous stage.

2. The VAT exemption certificate attached as an annex is used to confirm that the transaction meets the requirements for VAT exemption under this regulation. This certificate is stamped by the competent authorities of the Member State of the entity acquiring the defense products or other products intended for defense purposes in the context of contracts resulting from acquisitions benefiting from the support of the SAFE instrument and must be kept by the supplier of these products in their records.

The Commission uses a secure exchange system to facilitate the exchange of classified and sensitive information between the Commission and the Member States, as well as, where appropriate, with contractors or other final recipients.

2. The Commission has access to information, including classified information, strictly necessary for verifying the conditions of payment disbursements and for conducting the verifications, examinations, audits, and investigations, reports, as well as the controls and audits referred to in Article 14.

The Commission and the Member States may carry out communication activities to ensure visibility for the Union regarding the financial assistance envisaged in relevant European Defence Industry Investment Plans, including through joint communication activities with the concerned national authorities, while duly taking into account security requirements. The Commission may, where appropriate, ensure that support provided under the SAFE instrument is communicated and recognized through a financing statement.

2. Member States benefiting from financial assistance under the SAFE instrument ensure the visibility of Union financial assistance while duly taking into account security requirements, including, where appropriate, by displaying the Union emblem and an appropriate funding statement reading "with the support of the European Union - SAFE," particularly when promoting joint acquisitions and their outcomes, by providing targeted, coherent, effective, and proportional information to various audiences, including the media and the general public.

3. The Commission implements information and communication actions related to the SAFE instrument, the measures taken under this instrument, and the results achieved. Where appropriate, the Commission informs the European Parliament's representations of its actions and involves them in these actions.
This regulation enters into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
